marrow__BIOCHEM_CH19_Q011.displayText:
The red curve shows competitive inhibition: it reaches the same Vmax but requires more substrate (higher apparent Km).

The red line indicates an enzymatic reaction taking place in the presence of a competitive
inhibitor.

The graph represents the enzymatic reaction velocity in relation to substrate concentration. The
black line indicates the reaction taking place in the absence of any inhibitor.

In the presence of a competitive inhibitor, as indicated by the red line,
• Vmax remains unchanged.
• Km is increased.

In the presence of a non-competitive inhibitor, as indicated by the blue line,
• Vmax is decreased

• Km remains unchanged
Note:

Suicide inhibitors are specialized substrate analogs. They contain a chemical group that can be
transformed by the target enzyme. After binding to the active site of the enzyme, catalysis by the
enzyme generates a highly reactive group that forms a covalent bond and blocks the function of

the enzyme.

emphasis: The red curve shows competitive inhibition: it reaches the same Vmax but requires more substrate (higher apparent Km)

rationales.b: A noncompetitive inhibitor lowers Vmax without changing Km, so its curve would plateau lower rather than recover the uninhibited maximum.
rationales.c: Suicide inhibitors irreversibly inactivate their target after enzyme-dependent activation; the red kinetic pattern described is the reversible competitive pattern.
rationales.d: The curve’s inhibitor pattern is identified by unchanged Vmax and increased Km, which is competitive rather than no listed type.

marrow__BIOCHEM_CH19_Q012.displayText:
On a Lineweaver–Burk plot, pure noncompetitive inhibition raises 1/Vmax while preserving Km and therefore the x-intercept.

«~~ x

The red line in the graph represents ah enzymatic reaction with a noncompetitive inhibitor.

The above graph-is called the,‘Lineweaver-Burk plot' or ‘double reciprocal’ plot. 1/vo (vo - initial
velocity) is plotted versus \i/{S] ([S] - substrate concentration) and a straight line is obtained. This
plot can be used to calculate Km and Vmax as well as to determine the mechanism of action of
enzyme inhibitors. The x-intercept represents -1/Km while the y-intercept represents 1/Vmax.

In non-competitive inhibition, Vmax decreases (or 1/Vmax increases) but Km is
unchanged. Hence the graphs of inhibited and uninhibited reactions have the same x-intercepts
(converge at the same -1/Km) but different y-intercepts.

Note: An allosteric inhibitor alters the conformation of an enzyme upon binding. Enzymes
affected by allosteric inhibitors exhibit a sigmoid, not hyperbolic, relationship between Vo and [S].

rationales.b: Allosteric inhibition is a broad regulatory mechanism and does not itself specify the noncompetitive reciprocal-plot signature asked here.
rationales.c: Suicide inhibition is irreversible inactivation and is not the reversible Lineweaver–Burk pattern described by the keyed option.

emphasis: Allosteric modifiers commonly mediate feedback regulation by binding a regulatory site and changing enzyme activity

rationales.a: An allosteric effector does not desaturate the enzyme; it alters conformation and activity through a regulatory binding site.
rationales.b: Effectors can activate or inhibit, so their effect is not limited to speeding an enzyme.
rationales.c: Allosteric modifiers bind a regulatory site distinct from the catalytic site, then influence catalysis indirectly.

marrow__BIOCHEM_CH19_Q015.takeaway: Chymotrypsinogen is an inactive zymogen activated by selective proteolytic cleavage to chymotrypsin.
marrow__BIOCHEM_CH19_Q015.displayText:
Chymotrypsinogen is an inactive zymogen activated by selective proteolytic cleavage to chymotrypsin.

Chymotrypsinogen is a zymogen.

Some enzymes are secreted as an inactive form called as zymogens. The zymogens are converted
to their active functional forms by partial, or selective proteolysis. Examples of zymogens include
trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, proelastase, pepsinogen, prophospholipase A2 etc.

emphasis: Chymotrypsinogen is an inactive zymogen activated by selective proteolytic cleavage to chymotrypsin

rationales.b: Carboxypeptidase is an active exopeptidase, not the inactive precursor form of chymotrypsin.
rationales.c: A transaminase transfers amino groups between substrates and is unrelated to the chymotrypsin precursor state.
rationales.d: Chymotrypsinogen is not a clot-lysing protein; it is the inactive precursor of a digestive protease.

emphasis: Low-dose aspirin irreversibly acetylates platelet COX-1, a mechanism commonly described as suicide inhibition

rationales.b: Aspirin irreversibly inactivates cyclooxygenase rather than competing reversibly with arachidonic acid at equilibrium.
rationales.c: Aspirin inhibits platelet cyclooxygenase; it does not allosterically activate the enzyme.
rationales.d: The standard mechanism is irreversible active-site acetylation, not reversible allosteric inhibition.

marrow__BIOCHEM_CH19_Q017.takeaway: ATCase integrates pyrimidine and purine status: CTP inhibits it and ATP activates it.
marrow__BIOCHEM_CH19_Q017.displayText:
ATCase integrates pyrimidine and purine status: CTP inhibits it and ATP activates it.

.¢

Y fas

4

Both cytidine triphosphate and adenosine triphosphate target aspartate transcarbamoylase
(ATCase) for feedback regulation.

ATCase, the catalyst for the first reaction unique to pyrimidine biosynthesis, is a target of
feedback regulation by two nucleotide triphosphates: cytidine triphosphate (CTP) and adenosine
triphosphate (ATP). CTP is an end product of the pyrimidine biosynthetic pathway. It inhibits
ATCase, whereas the purine nucleotide ATP activates it.

High levels of ATP can overcome the inhibition by CTP, enabling synthesis of pyrimidine

nucleotides to proceed even when purine nucleotide (CTP) levels are elevated.
emphasis: ATCase integrates pyrimidine and purine status: CTP inhibits it and ATP activates it

rationales.a: CTP is a pyrimidine end-product feedback inhibitor, but it is not the only nucleotide named; ATP also regulates ATCase.
rationales.b: ATP activates ATCase and helps balance purine with pyrimidine synthesis, but CTP also acts on the enzyme.
rationales.c: GTP is not the pair of regulators identified for ATCase in this pathway; the relevant effectors are CTP and ATP.

sourceNotes: Source question/key: ED8 Biochemistry p. 303; explanation p. 314.

marrow__BIOCHEM_CH19_Q018.takeaway: Pure noncompetitive inhibition leaves Km constant and decreases Vmax.
marrow__BIOCHEM_CH19_Q018.displayText:
Pure noncompetitive inhibition leaves Km constant and decreases Vmax.

Noncompetitive inhibition has constant Km and decreased Vmax.

Noncompetitive inhibition occurs when the inhibitor binds at a site different from the
substrate-binding site. The structure of the inhibitor does not resemble that of the substrate and
the inhibitor does not affect the binding of the substrate.

emphasis: Pure noncompetitive inhibition leaves Km constant and decreases Vmax

rationales.a: Pure noncompetitive inhibition does not increase Vmax; binding of inhibitor reduces active catalytic capacity.
rationales.c: Km is unchanged in pure noncompetitive inhibition, so the option's decrease in Km is incorrect.
rationales.d: Vmax falls rather than rises, and Km remains constant.

marrow__BIOCHEM_CH19_Q020.displayText:
Compare kcat/Km in common units: option C gives the largest ratio, 200 s⁻¹ / 2 μM = 100 μM⁻¹s⁻¹.

: >

The highest tcatitic efficiencihis| seen when Km= 2 micromole and Kcat = 200 per sec.

Catalytic Stiency i is caleulated as Kcat/Km, where Km is inversely proportional to the binding
affinity of the enzyme and Kcat is the catalytic constant (Vmax divided by the total number of
active sites of the enzyme present). Higher values of Kcat and lower values of Km gives better
catalytic efficiency. Catalytic efficiency can be used to compare the performance of 2 different
enzymes in catalyzing a reaction.

Step 1: Km of each option after converting respective units to moles will be 10, 2, 2 and 4 (each
multiplied by 10-6) moles.

Step 2: The catalytic efficiency is calculated as Kcat/Km. On substituting the values in various
options after converting to moles, the values come out to be 2, 25, 100 and 50 (each multiplied by
106) M-1 s-1.

Some enzymes can be so efficient that they convert the substrate to product instantaneously. They

are limited only by the rate at which substrate diffuses towards the enzyme in a solution. These
are called diffusion-limited enzymes and their catalytic efficiency is as high as 108 M-1 s-1.
emphasis: Compare kcat/Km in common units: option C gives the largest ratio, 200 s⁻¹ / 2 μM = 100 μM⁻¹s⁻¹

rationales.a: This option gives 20/10 = 2 μM⁻¹s⁻¹, far below option C after expressing Km in micromolar units.
rationales.b: 2000 nM equals 2 μM, so this option gives 50/2 = 25 μM⁻¹s⁻¹, below option C's 100.
rationales.d: This option gives 200/4 = 50 μM⁻¹s⁻¹, half of option C's 100.
